scope._includedProducts: Used `product-research.md` and `ehi-export-report.md` scoped to CHPL ID 10914 and the Help Center article explicitly titled `EHI Export` for OfficeEMR; this article references OfficeEMR v2021 and the same family-wide data export zip set, so only OfficeEMR artifacts were included. Alternatives (ENTChoice, other iSALUS products) are not explicitly covered by the target EHI export page, so they were excluded.
scope._excludedProducts: Excluded only non-target modules documented as separate products/features: ENTChoice is referenced as a specialty integration, and the earlier `Data Export`/InfoDive articles are explicitly distinct from the `EHI Export` documentation. Alternative: include all iSALUS products in one abstraction was rejected to avoid mixing unrelated product lines. Certainty medium.
excludedProducts: Data Export (InfoDive) legacy CSV export feature
other iSALUS platforms not named in CHPL ID 10914 OfficeEMR export documentation
scope._versionsInScope: Used the evidence date in `ehi-export-report.md` (`Product: OfficeEMR v2021`, certification 2022-06-06) and artifacts dated with `...v1-oct2023`/`October 2023`; no separate version-specific branching was documented on the OfficeEMR EHI export page. Uncertain whether later OfficeEMR point releases alter artifact structure, so scope is constrained to the documented bundle.
versionsInScope: OfficeEMR v2021 (EHI Export bundle, 2023 downloadable artifacts)
scope.scopeNotes: Single-family abstraction focused on the documented OfficeEMR EHI export implementation (KnowledgeOwl `EHI Export` page and linked zip artifacts).

exportPaths._mechanism: Used `ehi-export-report.md` and screenshots showing the OfficeEMR report-portal flow (search patient, request export, download zip) plus `files.json` URLs; path is a user-invoked UI flow, therefore `ui_single_patient_export` was selected. Alternative API-only interpretations were rejected because no API endpoint was required to initiate this path.
exportPaths._container: The page explicitly describes a patient-level downloadable ZIP containing JSON files; individual output files are separate entity-level `.json` documents (e.g., `demographics.json`, `claim.json`, `vital.json`), so this is a multi-file bundle.
exportPaths._formats: Artifacts are JSON files per entity type and sample archive files are not CSV/XLS/PDF-only; therefore `json` best fits. Alternative mixed format was rejected because no CSV/CCDA/FHIR payload is required for this path.
exportPaths._standardProfile: No standard profile is documented for the OfficeEMR export payload (`files.json` and `ehi-export-report.md` describe proprietary schema files and a product dictionary); US Core/FHIR language is not used in the actual EHI export schema. Alternative: map to `fhir_us_core` was rejected because payload shape is vendor-native and not FHIR.
exportPaths._selfService: For single-patient export, staff with the `EHI Export` role can request and retrieve a completed ZIP directly from the portal (`ehi-export-report.md`), with no explicit support dependency in documented steps. Alternative that this path requires vendors to manually package each request was rejected due explicit immediate zip workflow.
exportPaths._operationalBurden: Scored as 2 (low-moderate): role-based portal access is required and there are explicit steps, but it is immediate and self-service; this is less burdensome than the practice-wide path with manual fulfillment.
exportPaths.notes: Self-service single patient ZIP generation; each file is an entity JSON array linked by patient-level fields.

exportPaths._mechanism: The same EHI page references a separate practice-wide flow (`EHI Practice Export`) requiring a request and delayed fulfillment (`~15 days`), so this is best represented as `ui_bulk_export`. Alternatives like api_bulk_export were rejected because the flow is documented as report-portal mediated with manual fulfillment.
exportPaths._container: Practice export is also delivered as a patient-coverage ZIP and described as `all-patient` export, not a streaming API or database dump, so `multi_file_bundle` remains the best container call.
exportPaths._formats: Practice export artifacts and sample data are JSON entity files, matching the single-patient flow and matching the downloadable artifact schema set; no alternate compressed CSV/API format is documented for this path.
exportPaths._standardProfile: No external standard export payload is described for this bulk path either; evidence still points to vendor-native JSON exports of internal models.
exportPaths._selfService: The request is initiated via UI, but completion depends on the iSALUS Data Export team, making this path not fully self-service from end-to-end. Alternative `yes` was rejected because delivery is operator-dependent and delayed.
exportPaths._operationalBurden: Scored as 5 (high): process includes manual team fulfillment and ~15 day turnaround, creating operational lead time and coordination burden. Alternative lower score was rejected because delay and dependency are explicitly documented.
exportPaths.notes: Practice-wide export path is intended for migrations; high value for archive completeness but lower operational immediacy.

documentation._hasDataDictionary: Used `files.json` (XLSX data dictionary) and `ehi-export-page.pdf` (field-by-field descriptions); both are explicitly listed as part of collected evidence. Alternative relying on schema-only documentation was rejected because schema descriptions are empty and the spreadsheet provides semantic meaning.
documentation._hasMachineReadableSchema: Used `officeemr-b10-schema-v1-oct2023.zip` with 80 JSON Schema files and per-entity schemas present (`results/.../OfficeEMR_B10_Schema_v1-OCT2023`). This is a machine-readable artifact. Alternative of manual text-only docs only was rejected.
documentation._describesFieldNames: JSON schema and sample files include per-entity property names for every exported object. Evidence: `demographics.schema.json` and `sample-export/demographics.json` show concrete field-level names. Alternatives requiring manual reverse engineering were rejected because field names are explicit.
documentation._describesFieldTypes: Schema files define JSON types (`string`, `number`, `array`, `object`) for fields, establishing field typing even if semantic constraints are sparse. Alternative of no typing was rejected by presence of schema.
documentation._describesFieldSemantics: Semantics are described in the XLSX dictionary and in the 56-page PDF (export references + data dictionary entries). `ehi-export-report.md` states these describe each data element. Alternative of schema-only semantics was rejected because schema descriptions are empty strings.
documentation._describesValueSets: The collected schemas use plain strings without enumerations and no value-set documentation was included in `files.json` description; this is especially visible in `demographics.schema.json` where fields like `gender`/`maritalStatus` are typed as `string` only. Alternative `yes` was rejected due missing code/enum metadata.
documentation._describesRelationships: Sample JSONs reference IDs and related IDs in multiple files (e.g., `claimId` patterns described in `ehi-export-report.md`), and the PDF also mentions linked lines like `price_estimate_line` to `price_estimate`. No formal ERD is provided, so relationships are inferred but not fully modeled. Alternative `no` was rejected because cross-file identifiers are consistently present.
documentation._describesKeysConstraints: Schema/metadata show key-like fields but no required/unique/foreign-key constraints or cardinality rules, and some nullable structures are underspecified. Alternative `yes` was rejected due missing explicit constraints.
documentation._describesSampleData: Used `export-311322-voct2023.zip` and unpacked `sample-export/*.json`; 58 files with realistic records show array/object structures and value examples. Alternative that no usable example exists was rejected by this sample archive.
documentation._sampleRepresentativeness: Sample-export contains many major entity files (clinical + billing) but fewer than all schema entities; some schemas (e.g., `statement`, `hie`, `immunization_registry`, several chart-share goal subfiles) may be absent simply due empty test patient data. Evidence is a mixed set, so score kept conservative.
documentation._docsCurrentness: Artifacts and page metadata are dated (doc modified 12/19/2025, artifacts labeled OCT2023, and HTI-1 update screenshots referencing Q1 2026 additions), indicating maintenance in the last year. No formal changelog exists, so currentness is moderate rather than excellent.
documentation._maturity: Combined machine-readable schema, human-readable field dictionary, and sample export improve implementability materially; however, missing enums, inconsistent date typing, and weak relationship/key constraint details prevent top-tier rating.
documentation.notes: Very good field-level coverage package overall; strongest remaining gap is semantic precision (value sets and formal constraints).

fidelityRisk._representationType: Evidence includes an OfficeEMR-native JSON per-entity model and no external API projection wrapper, plus field names tied to OfficeEMR concepts; therefore native model-like representation is most likely. Alternatives external_standard_projection and vendor projection were rejected due file-level model fidelity.
fidelityRisk._mappingTarget: No standard model transformation target is documented for the EHI export output, so mapping target is `none` rather than FHIR/CCDA/flat tables.
fidelityRisk._projectionLossRisk: The export includes broad clinical + PM domains and many specialty files, and sample plus dictionary indicate comprehensive breadth. Potential omissions (telehealth/fax/intake/portal logs) are possible but not shown as primary schema gaps; risk estimated moderate-low.
fidelityRisk._conflationRisk: There are specialized entities for many workflows (e.g., dialysis, chronic care management, template encounter sub-entities), reducing obvious flattening. Some unknown specialty/custom form detail is still possible, so risk is low-moderate.
fidelityRisk._reconstructionDifficulty: A consumer can rebuild patient-level records from linked arrays, but full reconstruction requires inferred join logic and interpretation of coded strings without value sets. So difficulty is moderate, not trivial.
fidelityRisk._keyLossPatterns: Potential loss patterns are limited by absence of explicit value-set/constraint docs, date-format heterogeneity, and minimal relationship metadata. There is no indication of wholesale omission of core EHR domains.
keyLossPatterns: No formal value-set documentation for coded fields
Inconsistent date/nullable conventions may lose semantic fidelity during import
fidelityRisk._likelyOmittedAreas: Based on missing entities in schema and product feature set, likely underrepresented areas are telehealth visit artifacts, digital intake payloads, fax/image transmission metadata, and potentially custom module forms where mapping may be proprietary. This is inferred from feature lists in research and explicit absence in export dictionary.
likelyOmittedAreas: Patient portal interaction logs beyond messaging
Fax and custom document payload details beyond image metadata

accessConstraints._docsPubliclyAccessible: The EHI export documentation page and PDF were directly accessible via curl with no auth (`ehi-export-report.md`, `files.json`); downloadable artifacts are on public CDN links. Alternative that content is restricted was rejected by successful unauthenticated access.
accessConstraints._roleRestricted: The documentation is public, but the actual run of exports requires logged-in role permissions (`EHI Export` / `EHI Practice Export`) as described in the report. This is an access constraint for operational export execution rather than documentation availability.
accessConstraints._vendorInvolvementNeeded: Single-patient path is self-initiated; practice export explicitly routes to iSALUS Data Export team with ~15 day turn, so involvement is path-dependent. Alternative `no` was rejected for all-patients, and `yes` was rejected for single-patient; thus overall uncertainty remains.
accessConstraints._potentialFeesForStandardExport: No fee schedule for standard EHI exports was identified in evidence; only standard software pricing appears in marketing materials. Absence of explicit fee claims led to conservative `unknown`. Alternative `no` was rejected because non-discount or support-facilitated pricing was not verified.
accessConstraints._practicalAccessibilityScore: Public docs and direct URLs lower friction, but role requirements and a 15-day manual practice-export dependency introduce moderate friction overall; scored conservatively above low.
accessConstraints.notes: Best usability for single-patient export; practice exports require manual fulfillment workflow.

overall._posture: Most indicators point to broad, genuinely OfficeEMR-native (b)(10)-adjacent export coverage across clinical and billing domains, but several key implementation details remain weak (value sets, full domain certainty, formal constraints), so posture is `usable_but_partial` not projection-limited.
overall._completenessScore: Given broad entity coverage and explicit PM + clinical domains, completeness is moderate. Conservatively avoided 'comprehensive' because some modules (telehealth/fax/intake/custom forms) are unclear and constraints/values are incomplete.
overall._technicalUsabilityScore: The triad of schema, dictionary, and sample archive improves implementation speed; however missing enums and weak relationship formalization reduce automatic import confidence.
overall._confidence: Evidence quality is good-to-strong for core domains but uneven for edge modules. Confidence is conservative due unresolved non-core module coverage.
overall._strongestSignal: Conservative assessment is anchored by 80+ schema files, data dictionary XLSX, and a realistic single-patient sample export that align with documented `EHI Export` scope and multiple non-FHIR clinical and billing entities.
overall.strongestSignal: Presence of machine-readable schema + human-readable dictionary + sample export aligned by domain.
overall._biggestRisk: The main risk is silent partiality in areas not explicitly represented in the export dictionary (telehealth/fax/portal telemetry/custom forms), plus absent coded-value semantics which can produce downstream mapping errors.
overall.biggestRisk: Potential gap coverage for non-core workflows and weak constraints/value sets.
overall._summary: OfficeEMR provides a broad native JSON EHI export surface with good evidence of model breadth across patient, clinical, and billing domains; practical usability is strongest for single-patient export while bulk export has high process overhead and both paths still need stronger semantics for lossless migration.
overall.summary: Broad native EHI export with stronger coverage than pure USCDI/FHIR-only approaches, but implementation confidence is limited by limited constraint/value-set and relationship formalization.

notableFacts: OfficeEMR EHI export is served as zipped per-entity JSON files (proprietary model), not FHIR NDJSON or C-CDA.
Two operational modes are documented: immediate single-patient export and delayed practice-wide export (~15 days) requiring Data Export team fulfillment.
Export artifacts include 80 JSON schemas, an Excel data dictionary, and 58-file single-patient sample export.
Documentation describes billing, scheduling, claims, payments, and clinical encounters/notes, but does not provide code system/enumeration dictionaries.
